datasets.name: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a repeated awakening study of propofol sedation. It examines whether EEG complexity measures can capture dreaming and subjective experience during sedation. Recordings cover wakeful eyes-open and eyes-closed rest, sedation rest, and one-minute resting periods preceding each awakening, with some sessions including transcranial magnetic stimulation.
datasets.authors: Imad J. Bajwa1, Andre S. Nilsen1, René Skukies1,3, Arnfinn Aamodt1, Gernot Ernst2, Johan F. Storm1, Bjørn E. Juel1,2

datasets.name: Alphabetic Decision Task (Arial Light Font)
datasets.description: EEG dataset from an alphabetic decision task in which participants viewed letter stimuli rendered in the Arial Light font. It was collected to study sub-letter orthographic processing and to test optimal transport as a model of letter similarity. The dataset includes BIDS-formatted EEG recordings joined with behavioural data, stimulus information, and metadata, plus notes on recording issues and corrections.
datasets.authors: Jack E. Taylor, Rasmus Sinn, Cosimo Iaia, Christian J. Fiebach

datasets.name: Electroencephalographic responses to the number of objects in partially occluded and uncovered scenes
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 23 participants performing a passive viewing task with partially occluded and subsequently uncovered scenes containing game pieces on a game board. Conditions varied the number of initially visible pieces (4 or 32) and the number of pieces revealed after the occluder was removed (0 to 32). The dataset supports investigation of neural responses to object numerosity in occluded and uncovered visual scenes.
datasets.authors: Cemre Baykan, Alexander C. Schütz

datasets.name: The "Podcast" ECoG dataset
datasets.description: The "Podcast" ECoG dataset contains intracranial electrocorticography recordings from 9 participants (1,330 grid, depth, and strip electrodes) who listened to a 30-minute naturalistic story containing over 5,000 words. It supports modeling of neural activity underlying natural narrative comprehension. The release includes raw data, a minimally preprocessed high-gamma version, the auditory stimulus, an aligned word-level transcript, and linguistic features ranging from acoustic properties to large language model embeddings. Tutorials replicating previous findings are also provided.
datasets.authors: Zaid Zada, Samuel A. Nastase, Bobbi Aubrey, Itamar Jalon, Ariel Goldstein, Sebastian Michelmann, Haocheng Wang, Liat Hasenfratz, Werner Doyle, Daniel Friedman, Patricia Dugan, Lucia Melloni, Sasha Devore, Orrin Devinsky, Adeen Flinker, Uri Hasson

datasets.name: Expectation of Conflict Stimuli
datasets.description: This dataset, titled Expectation of Conflict Stimuli, accompanies a study of how the brain forms expectations about upcoming conflict and adapts to it. It is associated with research on the role of lateral prefrontal theta oscillations in a computational mechanism underlying conflict expectation and adaptation. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: María Paz Martínez-Molina, Alejandra Figueroa-Vargas, Francisco Zamorano, Pablo Billeke

datasets.name: Neural associations between fingerspelling, print, and signs: An ERP priming study with deaf readers
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a masked-priming-style ERP study examining neural associations between fingerspelling, printed English words, and American Sign Language signs in deaf readers. Participants viewed 300 prime-target pairs in which primes were English words, ASL signs, or fingerspelled words, followed by four-letter English word targets, while performing an animal-detection task. The data support investigation of cross-modal and cross-script priming effects in deaf readers.
datasets.authors: Brittany Lee, Sofia E. Ortega, Priscilla M. Martinez, Katherine J. Midgley, Phillip J. Holcomb, Karen Emmorey

datasets.name: Categorized Free Recall with Closed-Loop Stimulation at Encoding (Encoding Classifier)
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial electrophysiology (iEEG) recordings from a categorized free recall task with closed-loop electrical stimulation during encoding. Participants studied lists of semantically categorized words, completed arithmetic distractors, and freely recalled the words. Stimulation was triggered by a classifier trained on each participant's prior encoding data to predict subsequent recall. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Free Recall with Closed-Loop Stimulation at Encoding (Encoding Classifier)
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a delayed free recall task with closed-loop electrical stimulation delivered during word encoding. A logistic regression classifier trained on participants' prior free recall sessions predicts subsequent recall from encoding-period neural activity, and stimulation is triggered when predicted recall is low. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: The Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS) dataset
datasets.description: The Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS) dataset contains 128 nights of simultaneous recordings from a clinical polysomnography (PSG) system (Micromed Brain Quick Plus Evolution) and a wearable forehead EEG headband (Bitbrain). Recordings come from 108 adult participants drawn from the general population. Sleep stages were labeled by consensus of three expert scorers following AASM criteria, and AI-generated labels are provided for both PSG and headband data. The dataset supports validating wearable EEG against the PSG standard and developing automatic sleep scoring.
datasets.authors: Eduardo López-Larraz, María Sierra-Torralba, Sergio Clemente, Galit Fierro, David Oriol, Javier Minguez, Luis Montesano, Jens G. Klinzing

datasets.name: Auditory naming
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG recordings from 106 patients performing an auditory descriptive naming task. Electrode coordinates are provided in MNI-305 space. The data support a dynamic causal tractography analysis of the networks underlying auditory naming.
datasets.authors: Aya Kanno, Ryuzaburo Kochi, Kazuki Sakakura, Yu Kitazawa, Hiroshi Uda, Riyo Ueda, Masaki Sonoda, Min-Hee Lee, Jeong-Won Jeong, Aimee F. Luat, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: EmoEEG-MC: A Multi-Context Emotional EEG Dataset for Cross-Context Emotion Decoding
datasets.description: EmoEEG-MC is a multi-context emotional EEG dataset containing 64-channel EEG and peripheral physiological signals (PPG and GSR) from 60 participants. Emotions were induced in two contexts, video viewing and mental imagery, and covered seven categories: joy, inspiration, tenderness, fear, disgust, sadness and neutral. The dataset is intended to support cross-context emotion decoding, and SVM baselines with L1 regularization achieved above-chance accuracy for binary and seven-category classification.
datasets.authors: Xin XU, Xinke SHEN, Xuyang CHEN, Qingzhu ZHANG, Sitian WANG, Yihan LI, Zongsheng LI, Dan ZHANG, Mingming ZHANG, Quanying LIU

datasets.name: Depotentiation of emotional reactivity using TMR during REM sleep
datasets.description: This dataset contains fMRI, polysomnography (EEG/EMG/EOG), ECG and pulse oximetry, and behavioural data from a study of Targeted Memory Reactivation (TMR) during REM sleep and its effect on emotional reactivity. Participants rated the arousal of 48 affective images paired with matching sounds, and half of the sounds were cued during overnight REM sleep. Arousal ratings and heart rate deceleration were assessed at baseline, in an MRI scanner 48 hours later, and in an online follow-up two weeks after baseline.
datasets.authors: Viviana Greco, Tamas A. Foldes, Neil A. Harrison, Kevin Murphy, Marta Wawrzuta, Mahmoud E. A. Abdellahi, Penelope A. Lewis

datasets.name: Spatial Memory of Object Locations with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from epilepsy patients performing a spatial navigation memory task. Participants encoded object locations during guided navigation and later recalled them by self-navigating. Open-loop electrical stimulation was delivered to hippocampal and entorhinal electrodes during encoding on alternating, difficulty-matched trials, with no stimulation at retrieval.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Spatial Navigation Memory of Object Locations
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial electrophysiological (iEEG) recordings from a spatial navigation memory task. Participants encoded object locations during guided navigation learning trials and then recalled the locations by navigating to them during test trials. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Research data supporting 'EEG recording during playing MOBA game'
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 23 participants during resting states (eyes closed and eyes open) and while playing a real multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game. Events mark in-game occurrences such as kills, deaths, game start, victory, and failure, enabling analysis of neural activity linked to gameplay. Data were collected between April and July 2023.
datasets.authors: Hong-Zhi Li, Jia-Jia Yang, Zhen Lv, Li-Yang Wan, Wo Wang, Da-Qi Li, Dong-Dong Zhou, Li Kuang

datasets.name: Cued Recall of Paired Associates with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding or Retrieval
datasets.description: This dataset provides intracranial EEG recordings and behavioral events from a cued recall paired-associates memory task with open-loop electrical stimulation. Participants studied word pairs, completed an arithmetic distractor, and then performed cued recall. Stimulation was delivered to single hippocampal or entorhinal electrodes during either encoding or retrieval. Data were collected at clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Categorized Free Recall with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from neurosurgical patients performing a categorized free recall task. Participants studied lists of words drawn from semantic categories, completed arithmetic distractors, and freely recalled the words. Open-loop electrical stimulation was delivered to hippocampal and entorhinal sites during alternating two-word blocks at encoding, with stimulation parameters recorded in the event files.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Free Recall with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a delayed free recall task in which participants studied visually presented word lists, completed arithmetic distractor problems, and then freely recalled the words. Open-loop electrical stimulation was delivered during encoding to single electrodes in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, on alternating two-word blocks in 20 of 25 lists per session. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: PREDICT
datasets.description: PREDICT is an EEG dataset mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds005486). It was collected by a group studying pain and sensorimotor neuroscience, and it is shared in BIDS format under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Nahian S. Chowdhury, Chuan Bi, Andrew J. Furman, Alan KI Chiang, Patrick Skippen, Emily Si, Samantha K Millard, Sarah M. Margerison, Darrah Spies, Michael L. Keaser, Joyce T. Da Silva, Shuo Chen, Siobhan M. Schabrun, David A. Seminowicz

datasets.name: STReEF
datasets.description: STReEF is an intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset of 13 patients with focal epilepsy, drawn from the RESPect (Registry for Epilepsy Surgery Patients) database at the University Medical Center Utrecht. Five patients were recorded with electrocorticography and eight with stereo-EEG during long-term monitoring. The recordings include clinical single pulse electrical stimulation (SPES) sessions and support studies of structural and effective brain connectivity in focal epilepsy.
datasets.authors: Jelsma S.B., Zijlmans M., Heijink I.B., Hoefnagels F.W.A., Raemakers M, Bourez-Swart M.D., Otte W.M, van Blooijs D., van Klink N.E.C.
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.6.0

datasets.name: Auditory oddball comparison (Optimum-1, Learning-oddball, and the local–global paradigm)
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from 15 participants who each completed three auditory oddball sequences: the Optimum-1 paradigm for mismatch negativity (MMN), a learning-oddball paradigm for P3b, and the local–global paradigm for local and global effects. The dataset supports comparison of within-individual sensitivity of MMN and P3b effects across specialized oddball sequences and the local–global paradigm. Corrected event files, stimulation sequence definitions and stimulus presentation code are included.
datasets.authors: Renate Rutiku, Chiara Fiscone, Marcello Massimini, Simone Sarasso

datasets.name: Fatigue Characterization of EEG under Mixed Reality Stereo Vision
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from participants viewing stereoscopic scenes in a mixed reality environment, collected to characterize visual fatigue. Participants watched 2 resting scenes and 15 movement scenes, each followed by a rating scene. The data support both resting-state and task-state analyses.
datasets.authors: Yan Wu, Chunguang Tao, Qi Li

datasets.name: Numbers
datasets.description: Stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) recordings from epilepsy patients at Oregon Health & Science University, collected while they were in the epilepsy monitoring unit awaiting seizures. Participants were presented with auditory and visual numerical stimuli, either symbolic (Arabic numerals and spoken numbers) or non-symbolic (dots and beeps). The dataset supports investigation of the neural representation of numerical quantity across modalities and formats.
datasets.authors: Alexander P. Rockhill, Ahmed M. Raslan

datasets.name: Free Recall of Word Lists with Repeated Items
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial electrophysiological (iEEG) recordings from a repeated-item free recall task. Participants studied visually presented word lists, each containing 27 encoding events drawn from 12 unique words repeated one, two, or three times. After a 7-second delay they freely recalled the words in any order. Data were collected at clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Semantic_conditioning
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a semantic fear conditioning task, collected to examine how awareness of stimulus contingencies shapes neural responses during fear conditioning. The recordings were used in an accompanying study by Pavlov and colleagues on contingency awareness. The data are organized in BIDS format with HED annotations.
datasets.authors: Yuri G. Pavlov

datasets.name: The effect of speech masking on the human subcortical response to continuous speech
datasets.description: EEG dataset of auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) recorded from 25 normal-hearing adults listening to continuous peaky speech from one to five simultaneous male talkers, plus click trains. The dataset was designed to characterize how speech masking affects subcortical neural encoding of naturally uttered speech. It includes raw BrainVision recordings, event files, and stimulus regressors.
datasets.authors: Melissa J. Polonenko, Ross K. Maddox

datasets.name: EEG frequency tagging reveals the integration of dissimilar observed actions
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating how the brain integrates dissimilar observed actions, using frequency tagging. The recordings are organized in BIDS format and were collected to study neural responses to observed actions presented at distinct tagged frequencies.
datasets.authors: Silvia Formica, Anna Chaiken, Jan R. Wiersema, Emiel Cracco

datasets.name: Delayed Auditory Feedback EEG/EGG
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and electroglottography (EGG) recordings with audio collected during speech production under delayed auditory feedback. The audio channel holds the delayed feedback heard by the participant, and the EGG signal was minimally preprocessed to correct phase delays introduced by the amplifier hardware filter. Per-trial delay values in the events sidecar allow the speech waveform to be realigned to the time of production.
datasets.authors: Veillette, J., Rosen, J., Margoliash, D., Nusbaum, H.

datasets.name: Open iEEG Dataset (Pediatric iEEG, Wayne State University and UCLA)
datasets.description: This dataset contains interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during sleep from 185 de-identified pediatric epilepsy patients at UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital and Children's Hospital of Michigan. Per-subject folders include channel information, anatomical labels and resection status, and participant-level outcomes and background information. Derivatives include high-frequency oscillation (HFO) detections from RMS and MNI detectors, along with bipolar iEEG data used in a related study.
datasets.authors: Yipeng Zhang, Atsuro Daida, Lawrence Liu, Naoto Kuroda, Yuanyi Ding, Shingo Oana, Tonmoy Monsoor, Chenda Duan, Shaun A. Hussain, Joe X Qiao, Noriko Salamon, Aria Fallah, Myung Shin Sim, Raman Sankar, Richard J. Staba, Jerome Engel Jr., Eishi Asano, Vwani Roychowdhury, Hiroki Nariai

datasets.name: Affordances of stairs
datasets.description: An EEG and behavioural dataset in which participants viewed images of scenes (stairs) and rated either their aesthetic properties (beauty, complexity, interestingness) or their appropriateness for a reading or social activity. The dataset investigates cortical responses to environmental affordances and the intention to act. It includes raw EEG, behavioural ratings extracted from EEG events, and the full stimulus set with identifiable file names.
datasets.authors: Christopher Hilton, Lilian Befort, Ronja Brinkmann, Matthias Ballestrem, Joerg Fingerhut, Klaus Gramann

datasets.name: TMNRED, A Chinese Language EEG Dataset for Fuzzy Semantic Target Identification in Natural Reading Environments
datasets.description: TMNRED is an EEG dataset recorded from 30 native Chinese speakers during natural reading of news headlines and short sentences. Participants identified fuzzy semantic targets among target and non-target items. The dataset supports research on semantic processing of Chinese in naturalistic reading and includes raw and preprocessed data in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Yanru Bai, Qi Tang, Ran Zhao, Hongxing Liu, Mingkun Guo, Shuming Zhang, Minghan Guo, Junjie Wang, Changjian Wang, Mu Xing, Guangjian Ni, Dong Ming

datasets.name: MEG: Major Depression & Probabilistic Learning Task
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from participants with major depressive disorder and non-depressed controls performing a probabilistic selection reinforcement learning task. The dataset was collected to examine the Reward Positivity and related ventromedial frontal cortex activity during feedback processing. It includes 90 participants, 52 with MDD and 38 controls, all screened using the SCID interview. T1 anatomical and resting-state data are planned to be added in a later release. Associated publication: Pirrung, C.J.H., Singh, G., Hogeveen, J., Quinn, D. & Cavanagh, J.F. (2025), Hypoactivation of ventromedial frontal cortex in major depressive disorder: an MEG study of the Reward Positivity. Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging.
datasets.authors: [Unspecified]

datasets.name: Naturalistic fMRI and MEG recordings during viewing of a reality TV show
datasets.description: A naturalistic neuroimaging dataset in which 30 participants underwent fMRI and a separate group of 30 participants underwent optically pumped magnetometer MEG (OPM-MEG) while watching a 25-minute excerpt of the Chinese reality TV show "Where Are We Going, Dad?". After viewing, participants answered comprehension questions and then rested with eyes closed for 15 minutes, which captured spontaneous mental replay of the video. The dataset includes anatomical scans and fMRIPrep-preprocessed fMRI data, and it supports studies of naturalistic story and social processing and of inter-subject correlation.
datasets.authors: Jixing Li, Yike Wang, Chengcheng Wang, Zhengwu Ma

datasets.name: Gaffrey Lab Infant Microstates and Attention
datasets.description: This dataset contains high-density EEG recordings from 43 infants aged 5-10 months who watched relaxing videos while seated on a caregiver's lap. The infants were part of a larger study on the impact of bias and discrimination on prenatal and postnatal maternal health and infant development. The data support investigation of EEG microstates and attention in infancy.
datasets.authors: Armen Bagdasarov, Michael S. Gaffrey

datasets.name: Fundamental frequency predominantly drives talker differences in auditory brainstem responses to continuous speech
datasets.description: Auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) were recorded with EEG from 15 normal-hearing adults listening to continuous peaky speech from a male and a female narrator, and to click trains. Speech was presented at each narrator's natural fundamental frequency (f0), at the other narrator's f0, and at a midpoint f0. Click rates were matched to the mean f0s. The dataset supports testing whether f0 is the main driver of talker differences in ABRs and whether the f0 effect resembles the click rate effect.
datasets.authors: Melissa J. Polonenko, Ross K. Maddox

datasets.name: Laser-evoked potentials in the human spinal cord and cortex
datasets.description: This dataset contains laser-evoked potentials recorded from the human spinal cord and cortex. It combines electrophysiological recordings to characterize nociceptive responses along the neuraxis. The data are organized in EEG-BIDS format and shared under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Birgit Nierula, Tilman Stephani, Emma Bailey, Merve Kaptan, Lisa-Marie Pohle, Ulrike Horn, Andre Mouraux, Burkhard Maess, Arno Villringer, Gabriel Curio, Vadim Nikulin, Falk Eippert

datasets.name: EEG Resting-state Microstates Correlates of Executive Functions
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from healthy young adults (165 recruited, 140 in the final sample) collected to test whether intrinsic brain spatio-temporal dynamics, measured as EEG microstates, relate to executive functions. Session 1 contains 5 minutes of alternating eyes-closed and eyes-open rest recorded with a 64-channel BioSemi system. Session 2 contains behavioral data from nine executive function tasks. The dataset supports correlating microstate metrics with mean z-scored executive function performance.
datasets.authors: Chenot Quentin, Hamery Caroline, Truninger Moritz, De Boissezon Xavier, Langer Nicolas, Scannella Sébastien

datasets.name:
Assessing sensitivity to semantic and syntactic information in deaf readers: An ERP
study
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from deaf readers who read sentences containing semantic and syntactic violations, used to assess sensitivity to semantic and syntactic information during reading. Event-related potentials were recorded while participants viewed 180 sentences presented word by word, including subject-verb agreement, semantic, double, and word-order violations alongside correct control sentences.
datasets.authors: Karen Emmorey, Emily M. Akers, Priscilla Martinez, Katherine J. Midgley, Phillip J. Holcomb

datasets.name: 95 By BP
datasets.description: EEG recordings from healthy participants receiving laser-evoked painful stimulation at four individually calibrated intensities (NRS ratings of 2, 4, 6 and 8) applied to the left and right hand dorsum. Each participant completed 80 trials (8 conditions with 10 trials each) and rated the perceived pain intensity on a numerical rating scale after each stimulus. The dataset supports investigation of the neural encoding of pain intensity.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: Picture-Word Interference Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains magnetoencephalography (CTF MEG), structural MRI, and behavioural data from 30 healthy young adults performing a picture-word interference task. Participants covertly retrieved picture names and judged whether each name ended in a target sound while hearing distractor words that were phonologically related, semantically related, or unrelated to the picture. The data support event-related analyses time-locked to picture and response onset, as well as source localization using individual anatomical MRIs.
datasets.authors: Hsi T. Wei, Farhan B. Faisal, Tamara Beck, Claire Shao, Jed A. Meltzer

datasets.name: UV_EEG
datasets.description: UV_EEG is an EEG dataset by Yukako Ito, distributed in BIDS format. It is mirrored on NEMAR from the original OpenNeuro deposit (ds005274). The README provides no further details about participants, experimental paradigm, or acquisition.
datasets.authors: Yukako Ito

datasets.name: Neural representation of consciously seen and unseen information
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating the neural representation of consciously seen and unseen information. The recordings were collected by Rodríguez-San Esteban, Chica, and González-López and are shared in BIDS format. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds005273).
datasets.authors: Pablo Rodríguez-San Esteban, Ana B. Chica, José A. González-López

datasets.name: NeuroMorph: A High-Temporal Resolution MEG Dataset for Morpheme-Based Linguistic Analysis
datasets.description: NeuroMorph is a magnetoencephalography (MEG) dataset with high temporal resolution, designed for morpheme-based linguistic analysis. It contains recordings from 24 participants, totaling over 17 hours of data, acquired with a 208-channel KIT/Yokogawa magnetometer system. The dataset supports research on the neural processing of morphology during language comprehension.
datasets.authors: Amilleah Rodriguez, Dan Zhao, Kyra Wilson, Ritika Saboo, Sergey V Samsonau, Alec Marantz

datasets.name: Surrey cEEGrid sleep data set
datasets.description: Overnight EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants collected in spring 2017 at the Surrey Clinical Research Centre sleep laboratory as part of a wearable sleep monitoring project. The dataset includes full polysomnography (PSG) and around-the-ear cEEGrid recordings, with most subjects having both from the same night. No alignment between cEEGrid and PSG was saved, so a best-attempt aligned derivative dataset is provided.
datasets.authors: Kaare B. Mikkelsen, James K Ebajemito, Maria A Bonmati-Carrion, Nayantara Santhi, Victoria L Revell, Giuseppe Atzori, Laura Birch, Ciro Della Monica, Stefan Debener, Derk-Jan Dijk, Annette Sterr, Maarten De Vos

datasets.name: Search Superiority Recollection Familiarity
datasets.description: EEG and eye-tracking dataset from 30 participants who searched for objects in real-world scenes or intentionally memorized objects in other scenes, then completed a surprise recognition memory test. The study asks whether the search superiority effect reflects purely stronger memory or also qualitative differences in recollection versus familiarity. The data include FN400 and LPC ERP components, remember-know judgments, and receiver operating characteristics. Behavioral data are split into encoding and memory testing phases.
datasets.authors: Jason Helbing, Dejan Draschkow, Melissa L.-H. Võ

datasets.name: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19)
datasets.description: The Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19) dataset contains overnight home recordings from 20 subjects who each slept four nights with partial polysomnography (EEG, EOG, chin EMG), dry-contact ear-EEG, and a wrist-worn actigraph. Ten of these subjects also completed 12 further nights with only ear-EEG, actigraphy, and a single EOG electrode. The dataset also includes sleep scoring, post-night comfort questionnaires, sleep diaries, and electrode quality-check markers. It was collected to develop and assess ear-EEG as a sleep monitoring platform.
datasets.authors: Kaare B. Mikkelsen, Preben Kidmose, Yousef Rezaei Tabar

datasets.name: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2023 (EESM23)
datasets.description: The Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2023 (EESM23) dataset contains overnight ear-EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants, collected at home between 2020 and 2022. The first two recordings per subject also include polysomnography (PSG), while the remaining recordings are ear-EEG only. Each recording consists of a pre-sleep video sequence followed by a sleep sequence, separated by subject-triggered markers.
datasets.authors: Yousef Rezaei Tabar, Kaare Mikkelsen, Laura Birch, Nelly Shenton, Simon L Kappel, Astrid R Bertelsen, Reza Nikbakht, Hans O Toft, Chris H Henriksen, Martin C Hemmsen, Mike L Rank, Marit Otto, Preben Kidmose

datasets.name: Chisco
datasets.description: Chisco is a Chinese imagined speech EEG dataset recorded from five participants (sub-01 to sub-05) across 5-6 sessions each on separate days. It provides raw EEG recordings, preprocessed data in fif and pkl formats, and the text stimuli used to elicit imagined speech. The dataset supports research on brain-computer interfaces and decoding of imagined language.
datasets.authors: Zihan Zhang, Yi Zhao, Yu Bao, Xiao Ding

datasets.name: Dataset of intracranial EEG during cortical stimulation evoking visual effects
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) recordings from 22 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing presurgical evaluation, capturing responses to 115 high-frequency intracranial electrical stimulations that evoked visual hallucinations. Each recording spans 21 seconds around the stimulation, with events annotated by stimulated contact pair, current intensity, and evoked effect, classified into 14 clinical categories. The data support identification of brain networks underlying visual symptoms and creation of symptom-related activation and connectivity maps.
datasets.authors: Andrei Barborica, Felicia Mihai, Laurentiu Tofan, Irina Oane, Ioana Mindruta

datasets.name: Evoked responses to elevated sounds
datasets.description: EEG dataset of evoked responses to noise bursts presented from loudspeakers at different elevations in a hemi-anechoic chamber. It combines two experiments, a deviant detection task with adapter and probe sounds and a one-back localization task. In the one-back task, a subset of participants was also tested with ear molds that disrupt elevation perception. Participants first completed a sound-elevation localization test, and behavioral responses are included.
datasets.authors: Ole Bialas, Marc Schoewiesner

datasets.name: EEG: DPX Cog Ctl Task in Acute Mild TBI
datasets.description: EEG recordings from healthy controls and participants with sub-acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) performing the Dot Probe Continuous Performance Task (DPX), a cognitive control paradigm. Session 1 took place 3 to 14 days post-injury, with follow-up sessions at about 2 and 4 months. The dataset includes task code and analysis scripts, and it experienced considerable participant attrition across timepoints. MRI was acquired only in Session 1 and is not currently included in this dataset; it is planned to be uploaded later.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: FACE-DEC
datasets.description: FACE-DEC is an OPM-MEG (optically pumped magnetometer magnetoencephalography) dataset for studying face perception through multivariate decoding and representational similarity analysis. The release includes analysis code for preprocessing (face_1_prep), decoding (face_2_dec), RSA (face_3_rsa), statistics (face_4_stat), and Bayesian model selection (face_6_bayes.m), with a main entry script (face_0_main). Individual facial point clouds and structural MRIs were not collected because optical scanning equipment was unavailable, so all analyses were performed at the whole-brain sensor level. Data collection was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Peking University.
datasets.authors: Wei Xu, et al.

datasets.name: 200 Objects Infants EEG
datasets.description: Infant EEG recordings collected while infants viewed 200 object images presented in rapid visual streams. The dataset supports investigation of the early development of visual object representations and includes analysis code for preprocessing, epoching and representational similarity analysis (RSA).
datasets.authors: Tijl Grootswagers, Genevieve Quek, Zhen Zeng, Manuel Varlet

datasets.name: STERNBERG DIFFICULT
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from participants performing a Sternberg working memory task with Russian consonant letter sets of 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 items. Each participant completed 200 trials across five difficulty blocks. Raven's Progressive Matrices scores are provided for each participant in participants.tsv.
datasets.authors: Natalia Zhozhikashvili, Maria Protopova, Tatiana Shkurenko, Marie Arsalidou, Ilya Zakharov, Boris Kotchoubey, Sergey Malykh, Yuri Pavlov

datasets.name: Proactive selective attention across competition contexts
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating proactive selective attention across different competition contexts. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds005089) and organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Blanca Aguado-Lopez, Ana F. Palenciano, Jose M. G. Penalver, Paloma Diaz-Gutierrez, David Lopez-Garcia, Chiara Avancini, Luis F. Ciria, Maria Ruz

datasets.name: rapid-hemifield-object-eeg
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants viewing object and word stimuli presented in rapid serial streams at 5 Hz to the left visual field, the right visual field, or centrally. Participants performed an orthogonal red target detection task while stimuli were shown. The dataset supports investigation of the temporal dynamics of visual object coding within and across the cerebral hemispheres, particularly for objects in peripheral vision.
datasets.authors: Amanda K Robinson, Tijl Grootswagers, Sophia M Shatek, Marlene Behrmann, Thomas A Carlson

datasets.name: Safety and Accuracy of Stereoelectroencephalography for Pediatric Patients with Prior Craniotomy
datasets.description: BIDS-formatted intracranial EEG dataset of stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) electrode data from pediatric patients with prior craniotomy. The data support an analysis of the safety and accuracy of SEEG in this population. Electrode coordinates are given in each individual's native post-operative CT space, with no alignment to other imaging modalities or standardized atlases.
datasets.authors: Peter H Yang, Nathan Wulfekammer, Amanda V. Jenson, Elliot Neal, Stuart Tomko, John Zempel, Peter Brunner, Sean D McEvoy, Matthew D Smyth, Jarod L Roland

datasets.name: The Effects of Directed Therapeutic Intent on Live and Damaged Cells
datasets.description: This case study records physiological and EEG data from a self-described practitioner of energy medicine who performed directed therapeutic intent on live and damaged cells. Across 60 double-blind treatment and control sessions, cell types (live, dead/x-rayed, or medium only) were randomized and concealed from both the practitioner and the experimenter. Matched control cells treated by a sham therapist provide behavioral measures of cellular outcomes.
datasets.authors: Lorenzo Cohen, Arnaud Delorme, Peiying Yang, Andrew Cusimano, Sharmistha Chakraborty, Phuong Nguyen, Defeng Deng, Shafaqmuhammad Iqbal, Monica Nelson, Chris Fields

datasets.name: Heuristics in risky decision-making relate to preferential representation of information MEG data
datasets.description: MEG recordings from participants performing a localizer task and a risky decision-making task, used to study how heuristics in risky choice relate to preferential neural representation of information. The dataset includes raw MEG with photodiode-derived event timing, event information tables, and preprocessed epoched data for the localizer and choice phases.
datasets.authors: Evan M. Russek, Rani Moran, Yunzhe Liu, Ray Dolan, Quentin Huys

datasets.name: Paired Associates Learning: Memory for Word Pairs in Cued Recall
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG and behavioral event data from a paired associates learning task in which participants studied pairs of visually presented words, solved arithmetic distractor problems, and then performed cued recall. Data were collected from clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania. Recordings include monopolar and bipolar iEEG with subject-specific electrode montages, MNI/Talairach coordinates, and brain region annotations.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: 40Hz Auditory Entrainment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from elderly participants with dementia during 40 Hz auditory stimulation designed to entrain brain oscillations in the gamma band. The stimulus was a 5 kHz carrier tone amplitude modulated by a 40 Hz pulse train, presented in short (six-trial) and long (ten-trial) sessions with interleaved rest. The dataset supports investigation of gamma entrainment as a potential intervention for Alzheimer's disease-related symptoms.
datasets.authors: Mojtaba Lahijanian, Hamid Aghajan, Zahra Vahabi

datasets.name: The effect of theta tACS on working memory
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a study testing whether theta transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) improves working memory. Participants received either 20 minutes of verum or sham stimulation (1 mA, 6 Hz, Fpz-CPz) and then performed working memory tasks requiring mental manipulation or simple retention of items. Resting-state EEG with eyes closed and eyes open was also recorded before the task.
datasets.authors: Yuri G. Pavlov, Dauren Kasanov

datasets.name: Tilt Illusion by Phase
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 36 participants performing an orientation discrimination task in a visual tilt illusion paradigm. A central target grating, titrated to appear vertical on average, was surrounded by an annular grating tilted by ±30 degrees. The dataset supports analysis of prestimulus EEG correlates, including alpha oscillation power and phase, of increased or decreased tilt illusion strength.
datasets.authors: Jessica G. Williams, William J. Harrison, Henry A. Beale, Jason B. Mattingley, Anthony M. Harris

datasets.name: Auditory naming task with questions that begin or end with a wh-interrogative
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during an auditory naming task in which participants heard questions that either began or ended with a wh-interrogative word. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and supports investigation of the neural dynamics underlying language processing and naming. It is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: Yu Kitazawa, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: Exploring the electrophysiology of Parkinson's disease - magnetoencephalography combined with deep brain recordings from the subthalamic nucleus.
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous magnetoencephalography (MEG) and subthalamic nucleus local field potential (STN LFP) recordings from externalized deep brain stimulation (DBS) patients with Parkinson's disease. Recordings were acquired with and without dopaminergic medication during rest, static forearm extension (hold), and self-paced fist-clenching (move). The project aimed to characterize basal ganglia-cortex loop neurophysiology and how it is modulated by movement and medication.
datasets.authors: Fayed Rassoulou, Alexandra Steina, Christian J. Hartmann, Jan Vesper, Markus Butz, Alfons Schnitzler, Jan Hirschmann

datasets.name: The Time-Course of Food Representation in the Human Brain
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw EEG recordings, organized in BIDS format, collected to study the time-course of food representation in the human brain. It supports analyses of how neural responses to food stimuli unfold over time. Code, figures and the associated manuscript are available through linked resources.
datasets.authors: Denise Moerel, James Psihoyos, Thomas A. Carlson

datasets.name: WIRED ICM Sample Dataset - Workshop on Intracranial Recordings in Humans, Epilepsy, DBS
datasets.description: A sample intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset prepared for the WIRED ICM course on intracranial recordings in humans, epilepsy, and deep brain stimulation (Paris, March 2024). It contains recordings from patients with epilepsy during naturalistic listening tasks (movie trailers and TIMIT sentences). It also includes illustrative examples of seizure-related activity and vagus nerve stimulator artifact.
datasets.authors: Liberty S. Hamilton, Maansi Desai, Alyssa Field

datasets.name: EEG data set for a architectural affordances task
datasets.description: EEG dataset collected during an architectural affordances task, in which participants experienced architectural spaces while brain activity was recorded. The dataset is shared in raw form, follows an unofficial BIDS extension, and is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds004980).
datasets.authors: Wang,S., Oliveira,G.S., Djebbara,Z, Gramann, K.

datasets.name: CARLA: Adjusted common average referencing for cortico-cortical evoked potential data
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (sEEG/ECoG) recordings from four patients undergoing single pulse electrical stimulation to elicit cortico-cortical evoked potentials. The dataset supports the development and evaluation of CARLA, an adjusted common average referencing method for cortico-cortical evoked potential data. It contains the raw data needed to reproduce the associated paper's results, except for figures 7 and 8, whose data are censored.
datasets.authors: Harvey Huang, Gabriela Ojeda Valencia, Nicholas M Gregg, Gamaleldin M Osman, Morgan N Montoya, Gregory A Worrell, Kai J Miller, Dora Hermes

datasets.name: ChineseEEG: A Chinese Linguistic Corpora EEG Dataset for Semantic Alignment and Neural Decoding
datasets.description: ChineseEEG is a high-density EEG dataset with simultaneous eye-tracking recorded from 10 participants who silently read two Chinese children's novels (The Little Prince and Garnett Dream), with about 11 hours of reading per participant in total. It includes raw data, filtered and minimally pre-processed EEG derivatives, and BERT-base-chinese text embeddings of the stimulus materials. The resource supports research on semantic alignment between language model representations and neural activity, and on neural decoding.
datasets.authors: Xinyu Mou, Cuilin He, Liwei Tan, Junjie Yu, Huadong Liang, Jianyu Zhang, Tian Yan, Yu-Fang Yang, Ting Xu, Qing Wang, Miao Cao, Zijiao Chen, Chuan-Peng Hu, Xindi Wang, Quanying Liu, Haiyan Wu

datasets.name: Braille letters - EEG
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from participants who received tactile Braille letters (B, C, D, L, M, N, V, Z) on Braille cells under the left and right index fingers. The dataset accompanies a study on how sensory representations are transformed into perceptual Braille letter representations in the visually deprived brain. Data are provided in BrainVision format with event files describing trial onsets, stimulus types, catch trials and pedal responses.
datasets.authors: Marleen Haupt, Monika Graumann, Santani Teng, Carina Kaltenbach, Radoslaw M. Cichy

datasets.name: SpatialMemory
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating visuo-spatial working memory (VSWM) for sequences during a computerized spatial span task in younger and older healthy adults. The study examines whether theta and gamma oscillatory dynamics reflect item-level sequence encoding and recall, and how these processes change in healthy cognitive aging. Results indicate that later gamma power during encoding and theta-gamma phase amplitude coupling during recall track serial position, and may be preserved with aging.
datasets.authors: Paul Kieffaber, Makenna McGill

datasets.name: Probability Decision-making Task with ambiguity
datasets.description: A multimodal dataset of human decision-making under risk and ambiguity from 53 healthy volunteers aged 18-31. It includes structural MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI), task fMRI, and concurrent EEG recorded during inhibitory transcranial magnetic stimulation over two parietal regions and the vertex. The data enable investigation of the role of the parietal cortex in ambiguity computations.
datasets.authors: Alejandra Figueroa-Vargas, Gabriela Valdebenito-Oyarzo, María Paz Martínez-Molina, Francisco Zamorano, Pablo Billeke

datasets.name: A Resting-state EEG Dataset for Sleep Deprivation
datasets.description: This dataset contains resting-state EEG recordings from 71 participants collected under two conditions: normal sleep and sleep deprivation. Session order was counterbalanced across participants. Recordings cover eyes-open and partially eyes-closed rest, and the dataset also includes measures of participants' sleepiness and mood states.
datasets.authors: Chuqin Xiang, Xinrui Fan, Duo Bai, Ke Lv, Xu Lei

datasets.name: Registered Report of ERN During Three Versions of a Flanker Task
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a registered report examining the error-related negativity (ERN) across three versions of the flanker task. The study evaluates experimental effects and data quality of the task variants, and the data are also used to assess the stability of performance monitoring over prolonged task performance. Recordings are provided in BIDS format with response-locked and stimulus-locked event labels.
datasets.authors: Peter E. Clayson, Michael J. Larson

datasets.name: pyFR: Delayed Free Recall of Word Lists, Preliminary Cognitive Electrophysiology Study
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a delayed free recall task in which participants studied visually presented word lists, solved arithmetic distractor problems, and then freely recalled the words. Data were collected at clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania. It is a preliminary cognitive electrophysiology study that precedes the FR1 and CatFR1 datasets.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Investigating the cognitive conflict triggered by moral judgment of accidental harm : an event-related potentials study
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 31 participants performing a third-party moral judgment task embedded in a semantic congruency (N400) paradigm. Participants heard scenarios describing intentional or accidental harm and judged whether a final target word was congruent with the scenario. Agent intention and semantic congruency were manipulated orthogonally to examine the cognitive conflict triggered by moral judgment of accidental harm.
datasets.authors: Flora Schwartz, Radouane El-Yagoubi, Julie Cayron, Pierre-Vincent Paubel, Bastien Tremoliere
datasets.eeg_reference: average of the left and right mastoids

datasets.name: iEEG on children during Stroop task
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from children performing a Stroop task, collected at Wayne State University. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and includes channel metadata and electrode locations standardized to the FreeSurfer fsaverage space. It is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds004859).
datasets.authors: Kazuki Sakakura, Eishi Asano

datasets.name: HID
datasets.description: HID is an EEG dataset in BIDS format with HED (Hierarchical Event Descriptors) annotations, contributed by Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, and Kevin King. The recordings are stored as EEGLAB files (.set/.fdt) with HED version 8.1.0 event annotations. The dataset is distributed through NEMAR and derives from an OpenNeuro deposit (ds004851).
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: T22
datasets.description: EEG dataset (TX22) from a simulated, semi-automated driving experiment using a leader-follower paradigm. It examines trust-based decisions about handing off and taking over control authority. The study tests whether real-time predictions of when intervention is needed can be used to give the driver feedback that supports active trust management. It builds on an earlier experiment (ARL_TX20) that used the same paradigm.
datasets.authors: Jason S. Metcalfe, Victor Paul, Benamin Haynes, Corey Atwater, Amar Marathe, Gregory Gremillion, Kim Drnec, William Nothwang, Justin R. Estepp, Margaret Bowers, Jamie Lukos, Tony Johnson, Mike Dunkel, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: T16
datasets.description: T16 (TX16) is an EEG dataset organized in BIDS format with HED annotations (HED version 8.1.0). It was contributed by Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, and Kevin King, and is released under a CC0 license. The record is a NEMAR mirror of the OpenNeuro deposit ds004843.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: TX15
datasets.description: TX15 is an EEG dataset organized according to BIDS 1.8.0 with HED annotations (version 8.1.0). It is a NEMAR-hosted version of the OpenNeuro dataset ds004842 and is released under a CC0 license. The README provides minimal detail on the experimental paradigm or participants.
datasets.authors: Gabriella Larkin, James A. Davis, Victor Paul, Marcel Cannon, Chris Manteuffel, Ben Brewster, Tony Johnson, Mike Dunkel, Stephen Gordon, Kevin King

datasets.name: TX14
datasets.description: TX14 is an EEG dataset collected while participants performed a local situational awareness task and simultaneously maintained supervisory control of a semi-autonomous vehicle. It addresses the shift of the soldier's role from active controller to system monitor and manager in autonomous military systems. The dataset supports study of trade-offs between local area awareness (target/threat detection) and vehicle control, informing dynamic task allocation in crewstations.
datasets.authors: Gabriella Larkin, James A. Davis, Victor Paul, Marcel Cannon, Chris Manteuffel, Ben Brewster, Tony Johnson, Mike Dunkel, Stephen Gordon, Kevin King

datasets.name: Dataset of electrophysiological signals (EEG, ECG, EMG) during Music therapy with adult burn patients in the Intensive Care Unit.
datasets.description: This dataset contains electrophysiological recordings (EEG, ECG, and facial EMG) from nine adult burn patients in an intensive care unit who received music therapy. It is part of a single-site randomized clinical trial. Each patient was recorded during two Music-Assisted Relaxation sessions, each with pre-intervention, intervention, and post-intervention phases. Pain (VAS) and anxiety-depression (HADS) measures were also collected to relate to the physiological signals.
datasets.authors: Jose Cordoba-Silva, Rafael Maya, Mario Valderrama, Luis Felipe Giraldo, William Betancourt-Zapata, Andrés Salgado-Vascob, Juliana Marín-Sánchez, Viviana Gómez-Ortega, Mark Ettenberger

datasets.name: Magnetoencephalographic (MEG) Pitch and Duration Mismatch Negativity (MMN) in First-Episode Psychosis
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from an auditory oddball paradigm with standard, pitch-deviant and duration-deviant tones, used to measure mismatch negativity (MMN). Participants were healthy controls, individuals with first-episode schizophrenia, and individuals with first-episode affective psychosis, recruited through the Pittsburgh Early Psychosis Program. The dataset supports evaluation of source-resolved MEG MMN as a potential biomarker of early psychosis.
datasets.authors: Fran López-Caballero, Mark Curtis, Brian Coffman, Dean Salisbury

datasets.name: Flexible, Scalable, High Channel Count Stereo-Electrode for Recording in the Human Brain
datasets.description: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings used to evaluate a flexible, scalable, high-channel-count micro-stereo-electrode for recording neural activity in the brain. The dataset includes raw and preprocessed (epoched) recordings from multiple species, including human patients, non-human primates, pigs and rodents. Direct electrical stimulation was used to examine the effects of stimulation on brain activity. Data are organized in iEEG-BIDS format, with binary files and channel maps in the derivatives folder.
datasets.authors: Keundong Lee, Angelique C. Paulk, Yun Goo Ro, Daniel R. Cleary, Karen J. Tonsfeldt, Yoav Kfir, John Pezaris, Youngbin Tchoe, Jihwan Lee, Andrew M. Bourhis, Ritwik Vatsyayan, Joel R. Martin, Samantha M. Russman, Jimmy C. Yang, Amy Baohan, R. Mark Richardson, Ziv M. Williams, Shelley I. Fried, Hoi Sang U, Ahmed M. Raslan, Sharona Ben-Haim, Eric Halgren, Sydney S. Cash, Shadi. A. Dayeh

datasets.name: EEG-attention-rsvp-exp2
datasets.description: Electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from experiment 2 of a study on how the brain prioritises task-relevant information during rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP). Participants viewed small objects overlaid on large letters, allowing neural dynamics of attended and unattended stimulus features to be compared. The dataset supports time-resolved decoding analyses of attention effects on visual object representations.
datasets.authors: Grootswagers, Tijl, Robinson, Amanda, Shatek, Sofia, Carlson, Thomas

datasets.name: EEG-attention-rsvp-exp1
datasets.description: EEG recordings from experiment 1 of a study on how the brain prioritises task-relevant information. Participants viewed rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) streams in which small letters were overlaid on large objects. The dataset supports analysis of the temporal dynamics of attention-dependent neural representations.
datasets.authors: Grootswagers, Tijl, Robinson, Amanda, Shatek, Sofia, Carlson, Thomas

datasets.name: Categorized Free Recall: Delayed Free Recall of Word Lists Organized by Semantic Categories
datasets.description: This dataset provides behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a categorized delayed free recall task. Participants studied visually presented word lists built from 25 semantic categories, completed arithmetic distractor problems, and then freely recalled the words. Each 12-word list contains pairs of same-category words from three categories. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: Pilot data for Loneliness in the Brain: Distinguishing Between Hypersensitivity and Hyperalertness
datasets.description: Pilot EEG dataset collected in preparation for a registered report on loneliness and its neural correlates. The study aims to distinguish between hypersensitivity and hyperalertness to social information in the brain. Further details on the registered report are provided via an associated OSF project.
datasets.authors: Joe Bathelt, Marte Otten

datasets.name: A Polish Electroencephalography, Alzheimer’s Risk-genes, Lifestyle and Neuroimaging (PEARL-Neuro) Database
datasets.description: PEARL-Neuro is a multimodal database of healthy middle-aged (50-63 years) Polish adults at risk of dementia. It includes genetic data (APOE, PICALM) for 192 participants, along with demographic, health, lifestyle and psychometric measures. A subgroup of 79 participants also has EEG and fMRI recordings during resting-state (eyes open and eyes closed) and cognitive tasks (multi-source interference task, Sternberg memory task), plus blood test data.
datasets.authors: Dzianok Patrycja, Kublik Ewa

datasets.name: Delayed Free Recall of Word Lists
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and intracranial EEG recordings from a delayed free recall task in which participants studied visually presented word lists, solved arithmetic distractor problems, and then freely recalled the words. Data were collected at multiple clinical sites in collaboration with the Computational Memory Lab at the University of Pennsylvania. Monopolar and bipolar recordings are provided with subject-specific electrode montages, MNI/Talairach coordinates, and brain region annotations.
datasets.authors: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: EEG data for paper titled - Precise cortical contributions to feedback sensorimotor control during reactive balance
datasets.description: This dataset contains electroencephalography (EEG) recordings collected to study cortical contributions to feedback sensorimotor control during reactive balance. It accompanies a paper examining how cortical activity relates to balance responses following perturbations. The data are organized in BIDS format with HED annotations.
datasets.authors: Scott Boebinger, Aiden Payne, Giovanni Martino, Kennedy Kerr, Jasmine Mirdamadi, J. Lucas McKay, Michael Borich, Lena Ting

datasets.name: Phantom EEG Dataset with Motion, Muscle, and Eye Artifacts and Example Scripts
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from an electrically conductive head phantom, used to test motion, muscle, and eye artifact removal with known ground-truth brain signals. Six conditions were recorded: brain-only, brain with eye, jaw muscle, neck muscle, or motion artifacts, and brain with all artifacts at once. It also includes the iCanClean EEGLAB plugin and example scripts for parameter sweep testing and validation.
datasets.authors: Ryan J. Downey, Daniel P. Ferris

datasets.name: Automatic Evoked Response Detection (ER-Detect) dataset
datasets.description: The Automatic Evoked Response Detection (ER-Detect) dataset contains intracranial EEG recordings collected during single-pulse electrical stimulation at the Mayo Clinic (Rochester, MN, USA) and the University Medical Center Utrecht (The Netherlands). It supports the development and evaluation of automated detection of stimulation-evoked cortico-cortical responses in epilepsy patients. The data are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: M.A. van den Boom, N.M. Gregg, G.O. Valencia, B.N. Lundstrom, K.J. Miller, D. van Blooijs, G.J.M. Huiskamp, F.S.S. Leijten, G.A. Worrell, D. Hermes
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.8.0

datasets.name: Dataset of intracranial EEG, scalp EEG and beamforming sources from epilepsy patients performing a verbal working memory task
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneously recorded scalp EEG and intracranial EEG (depth electrodes) from fifteen epilepsy patients undergoing intracranial monitoring while performing a modified Sternberg verbal working memory task. Encoding, maintenance, and recall are temporally separated. It includes electrode MNI coordinates with anatomical labels, trial-level behavioral information, and LCMV beamforming-reconstructed virtual sensor data for several cortical regions. The data support studies of working memory, connectivity, and replay of memory items.
datasets.authors: Vasileios Dimakopoulos, Lennart Stieglitz, Lukas Imbach, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: sfb_meg_phantom (B04/C01)
datasets.description: MEG phantom recordings used to characterize artefacts produced by deep brain stimulation (DBS) devices in magnetoencephalography data. The dataset is part of a larger study on device-specific DBS artefacts in MEG. It includes Neuromag phantom measurements, with movement onset captured by an accelerometer.
datasets.authors: Bahne H. Bahners, Roxanne Lofredi, Tilmann Sander, Alfons Schnitzler, Andrea A. Kuhn, Esther Florin

datasets.name: Le Petit Prince Hong Kong: Naturalistic fMRI and EEG dataset from older Cantonese speakers
datasets.description: A multimodal naturalistic dataset from 52 healthy older Cantonese speakers (over 65 years) who listened to excerpts of The Little Prince in Cantonese during fMRI and EEG sessions. It includes task-based and resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, EEG, language history and lifetime experience questionnaires, cognitive task scores, and audio/text annotations with NLP-derived word-level predictors. The resource supports research on language comprehension and healthy aging in a non-Indo-European language.
datasets.authors: Mohammad Momenian, Zhengwu Ma, Shuyi Wu, Chengcheng Wang, Jixing Li

datasets.name: Spatial memory and non-invasive closed-loop stimulus timing
datasets.description: This dataset contains behavioral events and electrophysiological (EEG) recordings from a hybrid spatial-navigation and free recall experiment in which participants act as couriers delivering items to stores in a virtual town and later recall their deliveries. Sessions were either read-only, used to collect training data, or closed-loop, in which classifier predictions of memory encoding were used to time stimulus presentation. It represents the non-invasive portion of a project aimed at improving memory through closed-loop stimulus timing optimization.
datasets.authors: Joseph H. Rudoler, Matthew R. Dougherty, Brandon S. Katerman, James P. Bruska, Woohyeuk Chang, David J. Halpern, Nicholas B. Diamond, Michael J. Kahana

datasets.name: sEEG Passive listening to natural speech
datasets.description: Stereo-EEG (sEEG) recordings from epilepsy patients with implanted depth electrodes, and in two cases additional grid and strip electrodes, during passive listening to natural conversational speech. Participants heard 30-45 s passages and answered a two-alternative content question after each. Data were collected between June 2018 and August 2019.
datasets.authors: Anna Mai, Stephanie Ries, Sharona Ben-Haim, Jerry Shih, Timothy Gentner
